comparisons.peer_topic: AI Software Ecosystem and Silo AI Acquisition
comparisons.peer_summary: To support its AI strategy, AMD consolidated AI teams to develop a comprehensive software ecosystem, improved AMD ROCm software performance, and acquired Silo AI Oy to accelerate AI model development and deployment on AMD hardware, leveraging Silo's software stack for training large language models.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AMD highlight AI deployment as a primary demand driver, but MU focuses on the resulting industry supply-demand balance and pricing recovery, whereas AMD focuses on its strategic execution within that environment through software ecosystem consolidation and acquisitions. MU states that "Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI... resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved," while AMD details its internal response: "To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams... to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem" and acquired Silo AI to "accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware."

sentences.text: Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.
To execute our AI strategy, we brought together multiple AI teams across AMD to drive development of a comprehensive software ecosystem spanning our full product portfolio.
The acquisition of Silo AI enables customers to accelerate development and deployment of AI models on AMD hardware.

comparisons.peer_summary: Quarterly net revenue may fluctuate significantly due to large or delayed orders from key semiconductor customers, particularly for AI and wireless applications due to deployment timing and seasonal variations. comparisons.comparison: Both MU and AVGO identify AI-related demand and deployment timing as key drivers of revenue fluctuation and market dynamics, but MU highlights a recovery in pricing and supply-demand balance in 2024, whereas AVGO focuses on the risk of significant quarterly net revenue volatility due to the timing of these AI deployments. MU states that "Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI... resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions," while AVGO warns that "fluctuations may be magnified by the timing of customer deployments" for products used in AI applications.

This is particularly true of our products used in AI and wireless applications as fluctuations may be magnified by the timing of customer deployments and product launches, and seasonal variations in sales.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product Demand and Margin Volatility Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: Product demand varies by market segment and is difficult to forecast due to macroeconomic conditions, consumer confidence, and technology trends; shifts from higher-margin to lower-margin products, such as the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors produced at external foundries, have decreased and may continue to decrease gross margin percentages.
comparisons.comparison: Both MU and INTC discuss margin pressure and product mix shifts, but MU attributes 2024 outcomes to an industry-wide pricing improvement and supply discipline, while INTC cites specific structural margin erosion due to shifts to lower-margin products. MU reports "substantial improvements in pricing and margins" due to "industry-wide supply discipline," contrasting with INTC's observation that "To the extent demand shifts from our higher-margin to lower-margin products... our gross margin percentage has decreased and may decrease again," specifically noting Intel Core Ultra 200V processors as a driver of decreased margins.

sentences.text: Throughout 2024, we experienced substantial improvements in pricing and margins.
We executed well on pricing and improved our financial performance significantly from the start of the year.

To the extent demand shifts from our higher-margin to lower-margin products in any of our market segments, as has been the case with the Intel Core Ultra 200V processors, our gross margin percentage has decreased and may decrease again.
Changes in the demand for our products have in the past and may in the future reduce our revenue, lower our gross margin, or require us to write down the value of our assets.

comparisons.peer_topic: New Use Cases and Emerging Technology Risks
comparisons.peer_summary: The company introduces products for innovative use cases like DGX Cloud, Omniverse, and generative AI, but demand estimates for these areas may be incorrect, creating revenue or supply volatility. While emerging technologies like generative AI have driven data center demand, their long-term trajectory remains unknown.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address the impact of generative AI on demand, but MU reports a realized market recovery and improved pricing in 2024, while NVDA highlights the uncertainty and risk associated with demand estimates for new AI use cases. MU notes that "Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI... resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved," whereas NVDA cautions that "Our demand estimates for new use cases... can be incorrect and create volatility in our revenue" and that for technologies like generative AI, "the long-term trajectory is unknown."

sentences.text: Increasing demand growth, driven in part by deployment of AI and mostly normal customer inventories, combined with industry-wide supply discipline, resulted in an industry supply and demand balance that substantially improved from 2023 conditions.
